newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New S.African black empowerment group formed.
newsitem.headline: New S.African black empowerment group formed.

text.p: A new black South African empowerment group with strong links to Malaysia has been set up to work towards black economic emancipation, the body's chairman said on Wednesday.
Don Mkhwanazi, chairman of the National Empowerment Trust (NET), told a news conference that the body would be formally launched in a couple of weeks.
"NET is South Africa's first collective economic empowerment vehicle that is fundamentally geared to broad-based black involvement and participation in the capital market.

"Capital will be assembled under a representative leadership grouping of the black population to ensure that blacks become active beneficiaries of the changing and expanding economic fortunes of the new South Africa," Mkhwanazi said.
He said NET's objective would be "actively pursued" by its business, investment and operating subsidiary NET Investment Fund (Pty) Ltd (NETIF) through carefully structured projects and investments.
NET's assets were worth around 300 million rand of which between 40 and 50 percent were funded from abroad.
Mkhwanazi said NETIF was considering several new ventures in the energy, mining and automotive sectors.
He said blacks owned large chunks of capital in pension funds through their contractual savings but they don't control or manage this capital.
"NET will aim to unlock and redistribute these assets and to broaden the ownership by blacks in the significant asset pool that has accumulated in South Africa," Mkhwanazi said.
NETIF has already entered into two joint ventures with Malaysian companies in the banking and shipping sectors.
In January, Killinghall (Malaysia) Bhd said it would take a 50 percent stake in NETIF's Southern Bank of Africa Investment Holdings Ltd -- the holding company of Southern Bank of Africa Ltd.
Killinghall said it would take up the stake for 50 million rand cash.
The other joint venture with Malaysian business would see the establishment of South Africa's first black-owned shipping company, African Maritime Corporation (Pty) Ltd (Afrimar).
NETIF and Malaysia's Perbadanan Nasional Shipping Line Berhad each hold 50 percent of the new venture of which the initial capitalisation is be targeted to be in excess of 250 million rand.
